chapter: Los Angeles, Ellington and the recording scene
title: Lester Young after the Army, and the union rule at the Capri
summary: Callender describes Lester's depression, his drinking, and the six-month union wait that kept him to specialty spots at the Capri.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Did he ever talk about it to you?

Yeah. He would tell me some of the things... At that time, I guess he'd... Well, anybody who smoked pot was considered a dope fiend. So he was considered a dope fiend! And naturally he resented that, because he wasn't! He was an ordinary person like the rest of us. I mean, who didn't smoke pot? I certainly did. Although at this point, I smoke very little of anything -- and drink very little of anything. Because I have seen so many guys, like... Well, I saw what happened to Lester, his frustrations and feeling bruised... And I guess it's true.

He was, you know, such a great talent who wasn't really recognized or rewarded for what he could really do. But he used to get a big punch-bowl and take a bottle of sauterne wine and a quart of gin, and put it in there, and that's how he'd start his day off.
From the time he came out of the Army?

Mmmm-hmmm, yeah. And he would eat very little. Although he was playing beautifully, and still played beautifully at that time. But I guess he... I don't know whether he had a death wish or what it was, but frustration, I suppose, had a lot to do with it.
But he was like a different person after he came out...
That's what I've heard people say.

Well, he was always... I loved him. He was a beautiful soft-spoken person who never seemed to get angry at anybody. All he wanted to do was to play his horn, which he did so beautifully. But we were working at the Capri at this time, and the union wouldn't let him... He had to wait a six-month period. So the band would play, and then he would come up and do a specialty. They called it a specialty, because he wasn't allowed to be on the bandstand
during the whole set -- which was some silly rule, but nonetheless it applied.
